newsitem.title: JAPAN: Excessively weak yen not welcomed by Japan -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Excessively weak yen not welcomed by Japan -- MOF.

text.p: An excessively weak yen is not welcomed by Japan, a Ministry of Finance official told reporters on Friday.
The official said: "Like an excessive appreciation...an excessive depreciation of the yen is not welcome."
He declined, however, to say at what level the yen would be considered excessively weak.
Asked if he thought that the economic recovery was stronger than markets perceived, the official said: "I think (so), on the basis of the data we have."
The official said Japanese economic data showed that housing construction and industrial output continued to be very strong.

He added that the supplementary budget for the current fiscal year, expected to be passed in February, should offset some of the effects of fiscal tightening when the sales tax is raised to five percent from three percent and special income tax cuts are discontinued.
Both measures will be formalised in April, the beginning of the fiscal year.
On currencies, he said that as a general principle authorities do not like excessive swings "on either side". He added that it was important that authorities conveyed a consistent view to the market.
Asked about fading market confidence in Japan's efforts to implement financial reform, the official said the "process (for) reform is set in motion in a concrete manner".

He said a blueprint for foreign exchange deregulation would be submitted to the current session of parliament for approval and that ministry advisory bodies were looking into possible reforms in the securities sector.
